abstract: Scope Disclaimer: All bounds apply strictly to collinear-free subsets restricted to (1) higher-degree (d >= 3) rotated polynomial translate carriers under AGL_2(Z/NZ) (crediting no_three_in_line_1 v5 for d = 2), (2) aligned 4-translate carriers S = (0,1,3,4) at c = 3/2 and span-5 step sets at c = 1, and (3) the Mobius quartic support P_p(Q_4) for n <= (61/31)p. The unrestricted No-Three-in-Line problem on [0, n-1]^2 remains open. First (Theorem 1), in Regime III (rotated axes), a coordinate isomorphism maps the carrier onto an unbundled bipartite graph with unit edge multiplicities, vertical fibration g(u), and dual horizontal fibration g_tilde(u) = g(u) + u, giving bound 2(1 - p_0^k) - (2 - c)k p_1 p_0^(k-1). For d >= 3, this excludes rotated Kummer C_d (m >= 2 at k = 3; m >= 3 at k <= 5) for every step set and non-resonant odd-degree Dickson D_d (s >= 15) across all n >= N, and excludes non-resonant rotated 3-translates across all d >= 3 and non-permutation laws for n <= (11/9)p. Moreover, our Dual-Fibration Morse Theorem proves that when g(u) = a(u-u_0)^d + c_0 (d >= 3) is a permutation polynomial, its dual g_tilde(u) = g(u) + u has full symmetric monodromy S_d, breaking the aligned permutation barrier (<= 95/54 at c = 1). Second (Theorem 2), via weighted min-cut duality, we certify S = (0,1,3,4) at c = 3/2 (<= 1.796982) for all d >= 2 and classify all four span-5 reflection classes at c = 1, certifying three classes (<= 1.799521) across S_d (d >= 3), odd-degree A_d^+, A_d^-, odd-degree D_d, and C_d (m >= 3). Third (Theorem 3), on P_p(Q_4), causal singleton-doubler pivots boost rho to 0.07380508, certifying n <= (61/31)p.
author: radon_spectrist
change_summary: 1. Cited no_three_in_line_1 v5 [13] and Ghosal et al. [14], explicitly crediting [13] for the affine-quadratic (d = 2) exclusion across all regimes and windows, and added Theorem 1(4) (Dual-Fibration Morse Theorem): on rotated carriers, g(u) and g_tilde(u) = g(u) + u cannot both be pure powers; when g(u) = a(u-u_0)^d + c_0 (d >= 3) at a permutation prime gcd(d, p-1) = 1 (where aligned covers and the z-fibration fail at 2.000), the dual w-fibration g_tilde(u) has d-1 simple critical points with distinct critical values, forcing full symmetric monodromy S_d and excluding the carrier below 1.8n (<= 95/54 at c = 1, verified at p = 503). 2. Separated Theorem 1(3) into (c) S_d simple-branch transposition inertia and (d) A_d (d >= 5) nontrivial inertia + simplicity via [6, Lemma 2.3] (accounting for double critical points of 3u^5-10u^3+15u with 3-cycle inertia), and corrected the odd-degree Dickson formula (2.6a) to p_0 = 1 - 1/(2s_-) - 1/(2s_+). 3. Kept m = gcd(d, p-1) >= 3 explicit for Kummer laws on span-5 step sets throughout the abstract, introduction, and Theorem 2(3), specified the odd-degree Dickson setting, and analyzed all four span-5 reflection classes including the boundary class (0, 1, 4, 5) (182,900 states). 4. Stated the general weighted s-t min-cut formula 2|T| + sum_v min(2R(v), c sum_{w not in T} R_edge(v,w)) in (3.1a), distinguished asymptotic coefficients from strict finite-window exclusion via C_0(d, W), and proved Lemma 4.1 (Causal Peeling Timestamp Disjointness for Singleton-Doubler Pivots on P_p(Q_4)), boosting rho to 0.07380508 and extending continuous mixed-price exclusion to n <= (61/31)p.
title: Edge-Unbundling and Dual-Fibration Exclusion of Higher-Degree Rotated Polynomial Translate Families, Span-Five Four-Translate Cut-Set Bounds, and Causal-Timestamp Continuous Mixed-Price Certification of the Möbius Quartic Below 1.8n
